en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section First Chapter
The Discussion on Past Aggregates and so forth:
Not Proven by Sutta.
Is the past an aggregate?
“Yes. “Then it must be said that the past exists?
“One should not say so,” and so forth.
Is the past a sense base?
Yes. Does the past exist?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is the past a constituent (dhātu)? Yes.
Is it to be said that “the past exists”? No, it should not be so stated …pe… Are the past aggregates, elements, and bases [existent]?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Does the past exist?
“One should not say so,” … and so on.
Are future aggregates [existent]? Yes. Are future [aggregates] existent?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is the future a sense-sphere (āyatana)? Yes.
Is it to be said that the future exists? No, it should not be so stated ... [and so on] ...
Is the future a constituent element (dhātu)?
“Yes. “Does that which is future exist?
“One should not say so…” [and so on].
Are future aggregates, elements, and bases [existent]?
Yes. Are they existent as the future?
It should not be stated thus … [as before] … Are present aggregates present as existing? Yes.
Are past aggregates past and existent?
You should not say so...
[and so on] ... Is a present base present and existent?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Does a past sense-sphere exist as a past thing?
You should not say so …pe…
Is the present element present as something that exists? Yes.
Is the past element past as something that exists?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Are present aggregates, elements, and bases present and existent? Yes.
Are the past aggregates, elements, and bases the past existent?
You should not say so… [and so on] … Are the present aggregates the present existent?
“Yes.
“Then you must not say that future aggregates exist as future.
… [as before] … “No, indeed. …pe…
Is a present sense-sphere present as something existing?
Yes. Is a future sense-sphere future as something existing? Yes.
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is it the case that a present element exists as a present thing? Yes.
Is it the case that a future element exists as something future?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is it the case that present aggregates, elements, and bases exist as something present?
“Yes,” you say.
“Are future aggregates, elements, and bases existent as future?
You should not say so … [and so on] …
Are past aggregates not present?
Yes. Are present aggregates not present? No.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is it the case that a past sense-sphere does not exist as a past thing? Yes.
Is it not the case that a present sense-sphere does not exist as a present [entity]?
One should certainly not say so …pe… Is it not the case that a past element does not exist as a past [entity]? One should certainly not say so.
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then is it not the case that a present element does not exist as a present [entity]?
You should not say so …pe….
Is it the case that the past aggregates, elements, and bases do not exist as the past? Yes.
Is it the case that the present aggregates, elements, and bases do not exist as the present?
It should not be said thus ...
[as before] ... Future aggregates do not exist as future? Yes.
Are present aggregates not present?
You should not say so …pe… Is a future base …pe… [not present]? You should not say so.
Is the future element ...
[and so on] ... the future aggregates, elements, and bases non-existent? Yes.
Is it not the case that one should not say: "The present aggregates, elements, and bases do not exist"? ... [as before] ...
Is past form an aggregate?
“Yes.
“Then does past form exist?
“One should not say so,” and so on.
Is past form a sense-sphere (āyatana)?
Yes. Does past form exist?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is past form an element? Yes.
Is past form existent?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is past form an aggregate, an element, or a sense-sphere?
“Yes.
“Does past form exist?
“One should not say so,” and so forth.
Is future form an aggregate?
Yes. Does future form exist?
It should not be said thus … [and so on] … future form is an *āyatana* … [and so on] … future form is a *dhātu* … [and so on].
Is future form aggregates, elements, and bases?
Yes. Does future form exist?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is present matter an aggregate? Is present matter existent? Yes.
Is past form an aggregate? Is past form existent?
One should not say so...
[and so on] ...is present form a sense-sphere?... [and so on].
Is present form a constituent element (*dhātu*)?
... [and so on] ... Is present form an aggregate (*khandha*), a constituent element, and a sense base (*āyatana*)? Is it true that "present form exists"? Yes.
Is past form a skandha, an element, and a base? Is it the case that "past form exists"?
One should not say so... [as before] ...
Is present form a skandha? Is it the case that "present form exists"?
“Yes.
“Then future form is an aggregate; future form exists?
“One should not say so,” and so forth.
Is present form an *āyatana*? ... [and so on] ...
Is present form a *dhātu*? ... [and so on] ...
Are present form, the aggregates (*khandha*), and the elements (*dhātu*) present form? Is it the case that "present form exists"?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is future form—whether as aggregates, elements, or bases—existent?
You should not say so … [and so on].
Is past form a constituent (khandha), yet past form does not exist?
Yes. Is present form a constituent, yet present form does not exist? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [and so on] … past form is a sense-sphere … past form is an element … and so on.
Is past form—whether as aggregates, elements, or bases—non-existent?
Yes. Is present form—whether as aggregates, elements, or bases—non-existent? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Future form is an aggregate; is it the case that future form does not exist? Yes.
Is present matter a *khandha*? Is it not the case that present matter does not exist?
One should certainly not say so …pe… Is future matter a *āyatana*? …pe…
Is future form a constituent element (*dhātu*)? ...
[and so on] ... Is future form an aggregate (*khandha*), a constituent element, and a sense base (*āyatana*)? Is it the case that future form does not exist?
Yes, it is.
Is present form—the aggregates, elements, and bases—not present form?
You should not say so …pe… Is past feeling … [not past feeling]? You should not say so …pe…
Is past perception...
are past volitional formations...
is past consciousness an aggregate?
“Yes.
“Does past consciousness exist?
“One should not say so…” [and so forth].
Is past consciousness a base? ... [and so on] ...
Is past consciousness an element? ...
[and so on] ... Is past consciousness an aggregate, an element, and a base?
“Yes.
“Does past consciousness exist?
“One should not say so,” and so on.
Is future consciousness an aggregate?
Yes. Does future consciousness exist?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … future consciousness is a base … future consciousness is an element … [as before].
Is future consciousness an aggregate, an element, and a sense base?
Yes. Does future consciousness exist?
It should not be said thus ... [as before] ...
Is present consciousness an aggregate? Is present consciousness existent? Yes.
Is past consciousness a *khandha*? Is past consciousness existent?
One should not say so...
[and so on] ...is present consciousness a *āyatana*?... [and so on].
Is present consciousness an element? ...
[and so on] ... Is present consciousness an aggregate, an element, and a base? Is it true that present consciousness exists? Yes.
Is past consciousness a aggregate, an element, and a base, and does past consciousness exist?
One should not say so… [as before] … Is present consciousness an aggregate, and does present consciousness exist?
“Yes. [The opponent asks:
“Is future consciousness an aggregate? Is future consciousness existent?
[The respondent replies: “One should not say so…” [and so on].
Is present consciousness a base (āyatana)?
…pe… Is present consciousness an element (dhātu)?
…pe… Are present consciousness as aggregates, elements, and bases existent as present consciousness?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is future consciousness a skandha, an element, and a sense-sphere? Is it the case that ‘future consciousness exists’?
You must not say so … [as before] … .
Is past consciousness a constituent (khandha), yet past consciousness does not exist?
Yes. Is present consciousness a constituent, yet present consciousness does not exist?
It should not be said thus … [and so on] … past consciousness is a base … past consciousness is an element … [and so on].
Is past consciousness aggregates, elements, and bases? Yes. Is it the case that past consciousness does not exist?
Yes. Is present consciousness aggregates, elements, and bases? Is it the case that present consciousness does not exist? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Future consciousness is an aggregate; is it the case that future consciousness does not exist? Yes.
Is present consciousness a aggregate, yet present consciousness does not exist?
One should certainly not say so...
[and so on] ... is future consciousness a base?... [and so on].
Is future consciousness an element? ...
[and so on] ... Is future consciousness an aggregate, an element, and a base? Is it the case that future consciousness does not exist? Yes.
Is present consciousness not a present aggregate, element, and base?
You must not say so … [as before] … This is established by the Sutta.
Is it not to be said that past and future aggregates, elements, and bases do not exist? Yes, they do not exist.
But has it not been said by the Blessed One:
“There are these three, monks, ways of speech, ways of designation, modes of description ... [as far as] ... for the wise”?
Is there indeed such a sutta?
“Yes, [you say] so.
In that case, it should not be said:
“Past and future aggregates, elements, and bases do not exist.”
Do you maintain that past and future aggregates, elements, and bases do not exist?
Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One:
“Bhikkhus, whatever form there is—whether past, future, or present; internal or external; gross or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near—all that is called the form aggregate (*rūpakkhandha*).
Whatever feeling there is… whatever perception there is…”
“Whatever formations there are … whatever consciousness there is, whether past, future,
or present … this is called the aggregate of consciousness.”
Is it indeed a sutta? Yes.
Therefore, it should not be said—
“Past and future aggregates, elements, and bases do not exist.
The discussion on past aggregates and so forth is concluded.
